findings.finding: New flag requires an enabled future horizon. Existing future guards plus constructor validation enforce half-open strict resources, node service 0 or 2 seconds, edge headway 2 seconds, q1 source clocks, canonical FIFO and actual EBS predecessor completion. The gap calculation does not silently accept heterogeneous durations.

Both original adjacent mask bits are feasible for the complete same chain. Their overlapping two-second windows form one free three-second union. On these fixed-duration calendars, lower_bound(A) and its predecessor give the nearest real right start and left end. Touching endpoints remain legal; the two consistency checks reject a contradiction rather than relaxing a collision.

The first positive-service static merge is selected once, including source or goal when applicable. Missing finite endpoints or failure of J:1->0 keeps the original launch; the implementation does not search later merges for a more favorable witness.

After the first-merge improvement, all positive node windows and every directed edge-entry window are checked. The first witness is reused once. Any known finite-gap increase vetoes the delay; unknown endpoints are counted and skipped. No horizon, current-time, zero, or infinity endpoint is fabricated.

Only the offset is changed, by exactly one integer second to an already-set bit. Existing exact whole-certificate validation precedes all calendar, reservation-ID, event, and task-lifecycle mutations. The original mask, last_push, first_clear, retry recommendation and diagnostic bucket meaning remain unchanged.

New witnesses, counters and policy wording are emitted only when enabled. Original earliest and selected launch are separate. Existing source decision timing includes the new work; added counts expose first-merge scans, resource lookups and actual neighbor visits. This read-only conclusion is not yet a default-off execution parity result.

limits: J is finite-gap packing loss for one local resource, not a count of feasible whole-route or q1 business slots. A finite gap may include elapsed time; the calculation does not establish actionable future capacity.

Known-gap non-increase does not cover unknown boundaries, future unannounced demand, source-head blocking, deadlines, or EBS release propagation. No throughput or THT improvement follows from this review.
